summary: All waves are integrated on branch perf-trial-20260906-030748 (hub). main is untouched. 52/52 tests pass (28 at baseline), and every optimization is guarded by a regression or tradeoff-pinning test.

The library's biggest cost was the dependency-free EPUB zip writer: a pure-JS CRC32 loop (Node ships a native one — 70× faster), deflate level 9 applied to JPEG scans that compress 0% at any level, and a final whole-archive buffer copy. Fixing all three took EPUB assembly of a 13 MB magazine from ~189 ms to ~7 ms and cut peak memory 26%, with output marginally smaller than baseline.

The interface's biggest cost was serial round trips: every REST call paid a fresh TLS handshake (no keep-alive), audiobook parts downloaded one at a time, and a magazine's pages/assets were fetched one at a time — a 300-page magazine spent minutes waiting on the network. Measured against a local latency-injecting TLS server: connection reuse halved a 30-request loopback run (each saved handshake is worth 50–150 ms against the real OverDrive hosts), and bounded 4-way concurrency turned 120 × 25 ms requests from 3.2 s into 0.83 s (3.84×).
One candidate was measured and rejected: lazy-loading CLI commands (≤9 ms ceiling, invisible next to process spawn). It stays recorded so nobody re-litigates it.

waves.name: Native CRC32 in the EPUB zip writer
waves.change: Replaced the 256-entry-table pure-JS CRC32 loop in src/epub.mjs with Node's native zlib.crc32.
tradeoffs: engines floor moved from >=20 to >=20.15 (zlib.crc32 availability) — done in package.json
CRC outputs verified byte-identical by the bench

waves.name: Store already-compressed media instead of deflating
waves.change: zip() ran deflate level 9 over every entry. JPEG/PNG/GIF/webp/avif/MP3/MP4/m4a/PDF payloads compress 0% (measured ratio 1.000 at levels 6 and 9) — they are now STORED, like the mimetype entry always was.
tradeoffs: A mislabeled media file (a .jpg that is really uncompressed data) would now be carried raw — in practice scan assets are real JPEGs, and the whole EPUB came out ~0.2% SMALLER than baseline (no deflate overhead on incompressible bytes)
EPUB readers accept stored entries (spec-compliant); unzip -t clean, and now asserted in test/epub-integrity.test.mjs

waves.name: Deflate level 9 → 6 for compressible entries
waves.change: Text/XHTML entries deflate at level 6: 2× faster for ratio 0.088 → 0.090.
tradeoffs: Text entries grow ~2%; whole-EPUB impact well under 1% because image scans dominate the bytes
One-line revert if the owner prefers level 9

waves.name: Single-allocation zip assembly (peak RAM)
waves.change: zip() built a chunk list then Buffer.concat'd the entire EPUB a second time. It now writes into one preallocated buffer (deflate first to learn sizes, then fill).
tradeoffs: Compressed entries still exist transiently (synchronous deflate cannot target an existing buffer). A streaming zip-to-file would cut peak further but changes the public API — left for the owner to want
During the rewrite an allocUnsafe EOCD zero-fill bug was introduced and caught by unzip -t; a test now asserts those fields

waves.name: Faster __bif_cfc1 page-blob decode
waves.change: read.mjs decoded every read-host page with a regex replace (per-match overhead at MB scale). Replaced with a hand-rolled code-unit quad-swap loop that is exactly equivalent — including the subtle rule that groups containing line terminators pass through and realign scanning.
tradeoffs: Equivalence property-tested against the original regex: deterministic hostile-input sweep + hand-computed edges (4n±k lengths, terminators) in test/read.test.mjs

waves.name: Parallel integrity-manifest hashing
waves.change: writeManifest() hashed files one stream at a time; now ~8 files in flight with 1 MiB reads, order preserved.
tradeoffs: Warm-cache gain is modest because SHA-256 runs at hardware speed on M4 and the cache absorbs I/O; the win grows on cold caches/slower disks and larger archives
Output is byte-identical to the sequential implementation — pinned in test/manifest-ref.test.mjs against a vendored copy of the old algorithm

waves.name: Keep-alive HTTP connection pooling
waves.change: REST calls used Node's default global agent (keepAlive off): every Thunder/stargazer/cover/page request paid a fresh TLS handshake. One pooled agent per TLS mode now: keepAlive, maxSockets 8, maxFreeSockets 4, 30 s keep-alive, noDelay, agent-level timeout backstop — with the per-request timeout/destroy handlers untouched so the historic wedge failure stays closed.
tradeoffs: Loopback understates the win: each avoided handshake is worth ~50–150 ms against the real OverDrive hosts
Up to 4 idle sockets per host linger ≤30 s; CLI exit closes them
Pinned by tests: reuse count, hung-socket timeout, 12-over-8 drain (test/http.test.mjs)

waves.name: Concurrent audiobook part downloads
waves.change: Spine parts download 3 at a time (mapLimit) instead of strictly sequentially. Skip/resume logic, per-part logs, fail-fast, and spine order preserved.
tradeoffs: 3 simultaneous CDN connections per title — deliberately low (the browser uses 6+)
Part-level failure still aborts the loan; resume unchanged

waves.name: Concurrent page + asset fetching (ebooks/magazines)
waves.change: Pages fetch+decode 4 at a time, then assets 4 at a time (both were serial — a 300-page magazine was 300 round trips). pageEntries stay in spine order for EPUB assembly; non-200 assets still log-and-skip; first page error rejects the loan.
tradeoffs: In-flight page/asset bodies raise steady-state RAM by the concurrency factor (bounded, a few MB)
Page logs now report decoded (completed) pages so numbers stay truthful under interleaving
Also removed: dead width variable in archive-read step 4

waves.name: CLI lazy command loading
waves.change: Considered splitting bin/libby.mjs imports per command. Measured first: the full import graph costs ~9 ms over the bare Node floor (36.4 vs 27.3 ms for libby help).
tradeoffs: Rejected: ≤9 ms upside is invisible next to process spawn cost; dynamic imports would move load errors from startup to command time. Recorded so nobody re-litigates it.

waves.name: Regression + tradeoff-pinning test wave
waves.change: Test suite grew 28 → 52. New: pooled-HTTP properties (socket reuse counted server-side, hung-socket timeout, 12-over-8 drain), downloadPart over pooled connections (redirect, exact bytes + sha256, truncated-body rejection with .part cleanup), EPUB spec validity via unzip -t, store/deflate method pins, stored-entry CRC pin, size-tradeoff pins (text still compresses <40%, stored media adds ≤1 KB overhead), manifest byte-identity vs the vendored sequential reference, and a proper fail-fast pin for mapLimit (the original lane test passed only by timing accident — the bug it masked was real and is now fixed).
tradeoffs: The EPUB size pins encode this campaign's CPU-vs-storage choices: if a future change re-inflates stored media or stops compressing text, the suite fails with the tradeoff in the message

adoption: Everything lives on branch perf-trial-20260906-030748 (hub), merged from lane branches -cpu and -net; each wave is an independent commit so any piece can be adopted or dropped alone. main is untouched.
To adopt everything: git merge perf-trial-20260906-030748 from main (fast-forward). package.json engines is now >=20.15 (zlib.crc32).

Behavioral deltas to be aware of: EPUB bytes differ from baseline by design (stored media, level-6 text) but remain spec-valid and ~0.2% smaller; page/asset log lines now report completions rather than starts; anything else is byte-identical (manifests, decoded content).
Reproducible: node --test (52), node --expose-gc perf/bench.mjs, node perf/net-sim.mjs src current. Lane notes: perf-notes-cpu.md / perf-notes-net.md in the respective worktrees.
